rubrics.criterion: Judge-set management — building the judge list (including defaults), verifying judge pages, tracking which judges are usable per scheme, and picking a judge per protocol — is performed by a dedicated owner type (class or cohesive module), not by the top-level facade class.
rubrics.rationale: Judge handling is one of the two drained responsibility areas of this instance; the task requires it to leave the facade and regain a distinct owner, and any sound repair must relocate this whole role regardless of the chosen class names or module layout.

rubrics.criterion: The per-proxy validation pipeline — DNSBL screening, per-protocol connect/negotiate attempts with retries (including the SMTP relay path), test-request building, response decompression, response validation, anonymity-level grading, and strict/non-strict type filtering — is performed by one or more dedicated validation owner types rather than by methods defined on the facade class.
rubrics.rationale: The validation engine is the second drained responsibility area; it must leave the facade as a unit, since leaving any stage of it behind keeps the absorbed behavior split from its true owner.

rubrics.criterion: The top-level facade class retains only discovery, queueing, limit, serving, stats, and lifecycle orchestration: no judge-verification or proxy-validation logic remains defined in its body, including the low-level request-building and response-parsing helpers that accompanied the absorbed engine.
rubrics.rationale: The instance's defining property is that nearly forty distinct behaviors share the facade; the repair is only complete when the facade's own method surface shrank back to its coordination role, not merely when some methods were made to delegate.

rubrics.criterion: The checking-configuration object stores the run's parameters (requested types, strictness, external IP, DNSBL list, negotiated protocols, request-method flag) and those fields are consumed by the validation owner that uses them, instead of the facade reaching into the object's attributes from its own methods.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state keeps the plan but robs it of an owner; restoring data-oriented design means the plan must be read where the validation behavior lives. A repair that only renames fields while the facade still interprets the plan from outside has not resolved the misplacement.

rubrics.criterion: The judge-management owner preserves the shared availability semantics: judge availability is process-wide state shared by all facade instances within one program run and is re-established on every search, so protocol checks observe the same usable-judge pools the original behavior provided.
rubrics.rationale: Availability semantics are the subtlest invariant of this instance (class-level state threaded through every run); losing the sharing or the per-run refresh silently changes when checks start and which judges are picked, so a correct repair must keep these observable semantics even while relocating the state.

rubrics.criterion: The search flow wires the re-homed owners into the run end to end: judge verification happens before proxy checks (with protocol checks waiting when a scheme has no working judges), and each discovered proxy is dispatched to the validation owner for checking with the run's plan.
rubrics.rationale: Relocation is only useful if the orchestration actually delegates; this instance's flow has a strict producer/consumer shape (gathering, queueing, checking, result publishing), and the association edges are exactly the call sites a repair must rewire for the new owners.

rubrics.criterion: The re-homed owners receive what they need — configuration, resolvers, loop, timeout, availability state — through explicit parameters, constructor arguments, or clearly owned attributes, without reading the facade's private internals or storing facade references to interpret run state.
rubrics.rationale: The injected coupling runs through attribute reach-through into another object's state; keeping that shape after the move would relocate text without repairing ownership, so the interfaces between facade, judge owner, and validation owner are part of the required work.

rubrics.criterion: No dead pass-through remnant of the absorbed code remains on the facade or in its owners: the repair does not leave behind forwarding stubs with identical signatures/one-line delegation, nor unused imports, module constants, or leftover state attributes that only existed to support the moved code.
rubrics.rationale: A mechanical hoist (move the body out, keep a one-line forwarder) leaves exactly this residue, and the two drained classes in this instance invite such debris; genuine cleanup means the traces of the absorbed placement disappear together with the logic.

rubrics.criterion: No duplicate or orphaned copies of the moved logic remain anywhere in the package: the validation and judge logic exists in exactly one place after the repair, and no old module-level helpers that were relocated keep existing as unused duplicates in their former location.
rubrics.rationale: This instance absorbed both class methods and module-level helper functions; a partial edit can easily leave the engine in two places. Uniqueness of the relocated behavior is an observable property a verifier can check directly.

rubrics.criterion: Protocol gating is not broken by the repair: when no working judge exists for a scheme (HTTP/HTTPS/SMTP), checks for protocols that depend on that scheme are still disabled for the run, the scheme's availability event is still set so waiting checks do not block forever, and the corresponding user warning is still emitted.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's most delicate behavior — cross-coroutine gating between the judge pass and proxy checks; naive extraction (e.g. moving availability to per-instance state, or checking judges after proxy dispatch) deadlocks or silently re-enables unsupported protocols.

rubrics.criterion: Per-run and cross-run judge state is not corrupted: a second search started after a finished one still re-verifies judges against the fresh external IP and does not inherit stale availability, events, or judge records from the previous run, and unlimited searches do not accumulate duplicate judges.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state keeps the reset-on-every-run behavior; a repair that moves the shared state into the wrong home (per-instance init, or lazily-initialized module globals) breaks repeated searches — a realistic regression specific to this code path.

rubrics.criterion: Public compatibility is not narrowed: the package's exported names (the facade, the judge and validation types, the serving types, the deprecated validation alias) remain importable from the package with their existing constructor signatures, so usage examples and the CLI keep working unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The drained types are still part of the documented surface (the deprecated alias even subclasses one); this case's boundary explicitly pins those constructors, and a repair that renames or re-parameters them breaks downstream users while passing the internal refactor's own tests.
